verdict_reason: The promoted kernel is the Grassberger-Procaccia estimator read in the SCALING REGION -- D2 = lim_{r->0} d log C(r)/d log r, estimated as the slope of the stable stretch of the log-log correlation integral -- which is what GP 1983 define and what every released implementation computes, and it reproduces BOTH of their published constants inside the intervals they state: on a fresh RK4 Lorenz attractor (N = 4000, 3-D state space) it returns 2.057784644364001 against 2.05 +/- 0.01 (+0.38%, R^2 = 0.99986), and on a fresh Henon map (N = 4000) 1.2013654838703887 against 1.21 +/- 0.01 (-0.71%, R^2 = 0.99986). It resolves dimension at the SHIPPED N = 100: uniform d-cubes over 40 seeds each give medians 1.9452 / 2.7548 / 4.1704 / 6.1007 / 8.5445 at d = 2/3/5/8/12 with 0/40 censored and correct monotone ordering, while iid Gaussian in d = 768 and 4096 is correctly REFUSED as `at_resolution_ceiling` (slopes 105.84 and 211.93 are emitted only under `_meta_..._raw`, and the headline is NaN). ON THE ESTIMAND QUESTION I WAS ASKED: removing the atomic switch entirely is the RIGHT CHOICE and I endorse it. Both prior forms were worse and I reproduced why -- `_atom_frac > 0` zeroed a whole model on a single repeated document, and a fixed `c0 >= 0.0025` cut made the meaning of the number jump discontinuously at an arbitrary boundary. Reporting the atom mass instead keeps the strict limit RECOVERABLE (it is exactly 0 whenever `_meta_correlation_dimension_zero_pair_frac` > 0) without letting a corpus artifact erase the geometry. I verified the one-duplicate case end to end: on five N = 100 3-cubes, inserting one exact duplicate gives atom_frac = 0.0002020202 and moves the headline by at most +5.8% (2.5062587474 -> 2.6526321831) and never to 0. BUT THE CODE DOES NOT COMPUTE THE ESTIMAND THE LEDGER CLAIMS: the headline is `_gp_correlation_dimension_plateau(distances)` on the FULL distance vector, so the atom floor stays inside C(r) and drags the exponent smoothly toward 0. Measured on a 1000-point 3-cube with a p-fraction collapsed onto one point: p = 0 / 0.02 / 0.04 / 0.10 / 0.20 gives headline 2.9139567040 / 2.5388433299 / 2.4040491472 / 1.9185886747 / 0.0008826996 (all status `ok`), while the SAME promoted kernel run on the atom-free distances -- which is the continuous-part exponent -- stays at 2.9139567040 / 2.9259615304 / 2.9522630596 / 2.9397674170 / 2.8375198722. I still score GREEN on the verdict axis, deliberately: what the code computes IS the GP estimator applied to the actual empirical measure, it converges to GP's own atomic limit of 0 as the atom mass grows and to the continuous exponent as it vanishes, no released implementation (skdim CorrInt, nolds) does anything different, and the case is unreached on real data -- I measured `_meta_correlation_dimension_zero_pair_frac` = 0.0 on gpt2, distilgpt2 and pythia-70m at the shipped defaults. The mismatch is between the code and its own docstring/ledger prose, so it belongs in `defects`, and the fix is one argument.
comparable_reason: Not comparable as shipped, on two independent grounds I measured. (1) THE SHIPPED KNOB IS INERT AND THE HEADLINE IS SENSITIVE TO IT. defaults.yaml:45 sets num_radii = 30, but both promoted calls are `_gp_correlation_dimension_plateau(distances)` with no argument, so the grid is always the default 60. On one 100-point 3-cube the plateau slope at num_radii = 10/30/60/100/300 is 2.7608469892 / 2.6561435088 / 1.9428882688 / 2.7690075888 / 3.3498714708 -- a 72% spread, and the configured 30 would give 2.6561 against the 1.9429 actually shipped, +36.7%. A knob that names a 72% range and is silently ignored is worse than no knob. (2) SAMPLE SIZE. defaults.yaml:43,46-47 give num_samples = 100 with pooling = 'mean', so N = 100 points, and `max_points: 2000` cannot raise it because mean pooling yields exactly one point per document. Fresh real-model headlines at that config are gpt2 5.4108068908, distilgpt2 5.9918865006, pythia-70m 5.6591887179 -- a four-model range narrower than the draw-to-draw spread prior rounds measured (sd 1.20-2.61 over forty 100-of-400 subsamples), so the shipped configuration does not resolve the cross-model ordering. Both are configuration/plumbing, not fidelity, which is why they sit here and not in the verdict.
github_reason: No code was released with Grassberger & Procaccia 1983 -- there is nothing to fetch, and that is a legitimate answer here rather than a gap. I therefore verified against the two things that do exist: the authors' PUBLISHED CONSTANTS (Lorenz 2.05 +/- 0.01 and Henon 1.21 +/- 0.01, both reproduced above on freshly integrated attractors) and third-party implementations. Against installed nolds 0.6.3 on a common delay embedding and a common radius grid, BLME's demoted percentile kernel is exact (prior round measured absolute delta 0.000e+00; nolds' own raw `corr_dim` differs only by its diagonal self-pairs). skdim's `CorrInt` is the closest third-party analogue of the promoted selector and is not a reference implementation of it -- on the separated-support mixture a prior round used as an adversary, skdim returns 2.8120 where BLME returns 2.5920 at the same N, i.e. BLME is CLOSER to the analytic 1 and, unlike skdim, converges (1.0094 at N = 20000).
paper_reason: Grassberger & Procaccia (Phys. Rev. Lett. 50, 346, 1983) publish D2 = 2.05 +/- 0.01 for the Lorenz attractor and D2 = 1.21 +/- 0.01 for the Henon map. I integrated both fresh (Lorenz by RK4 at dt = 0.01 with a 5000-step transient discarded, sigma/rho/beta = 10/28/8/3; Henon at a = 1.4, b = 0.3 with a 2000-step transient), subsampled 4000 points each, and ran BLME's promoted kernel on the pairwise distances: Lorenz 2.057784644364001 (+0.38%, inside the published interval) and Henon 1.2013654838703887 (-0.71%, inside the published interval), with R^2 = 0.9998572484 and 0.9998550473. Both are reproductions, not fits. Separately, RERUN_LEDGER.md's withdrawal of the logistic-map claim is correct and should stay withdrawn.
confounds_reason: Not a size or architecture proxy. Over the 51 archived models whose HF configs I could resolve, `correlation_dimension` gives rho(d_model) = -0.0775, rho(n_layers) = -0.0141, rho(params) = -0.0408 -- all null at n = 50. The mechanism supports that rather than merely fitting it: a correlation dimension is a function of the pairwise distance matrix alone, so an isometric embedding into any ambient width leaves it exactly unchanged (a prior round measured 2.858654049921 at widths 3/8/32/128/512, range 0.0). The one association worth recording is with VOCABULARY, rho(vocab) = -0.3226, which is expected because mean-pooled document vectors depend on how the tokenizer segments the shared corpus. The real dependence is on the POINT COUNT, not the architecture: the estimator saturates near 2*log10(N), which is why iid Gaussian in d = 768 reads 105.84 at N = 100 and is correctly refused.
defects: CODE correlation_dimension.py:307 and 285 (both promoted calls): the headline is `_gp_correlation_dimension_plateau(distances)` on the FULL distance vector, so the module's own claim that the headline is the continuous-part exponent is not what ships. On a 1000-point 3-cube (true continuous D2 = 3) the headline falls 2.9139567040 -> 2.4040491472 -> 1.9185886747 -> 0.0008826996 as the collapsed fraction goes 0 -> 0.04 -> 0.10 -> 0.20, all with status `ok`, while the same kernel on the atom-free distances holds 2.9139567040 -> 2.9522630596 -> 2.9397674170 -> 2.8375198722. Latent on real data (zero_pair_frac = 0.0 on gpt2, distilgpt2 and pythia-70m at defaults), but the fix is one argument: pass `distances[distances > 0]` when `_atom_frac > 0`, which leaves the slope of the continuous part unchanged since a constant divisor cancels in a log-log slope.

CODE correlation_dimension.py:220-224 and 385: `_meta_correlation_dimension_continuous` -- the key that is supposed to disclose the continuous part -- is computed with the DEMOTED percentile kernel while the headline uses the promoted plateau kernel, so the two are not comparable. On the same 4%-atom cloud the disclosure reads 2.1228436973 against 2.9855934052 for the promoted kernel on identical distances, a -28.9% mismatch. It is also NaN whenever `_atom_frac == 0`, i.e. on every real model, so the key is empty exactly where a reader would look.

CODE/CONFIG WIRING correlation_dimension.py:87 vs 285 and 307: the configured `num_radii` (defaults.yaml:45 = 30) reaches ONLY the demoted percentile helper. The promoted calls always use the default 60, and the headline is materially sensitive to that grid: on one 100-point 3-cube, plateau(num_radii = 10/30/60/100/300) gives 2.7608469892 / 2.6561435088 / 1.9428882688 / 2.7690075888 / 3.3498714708. Either wire it through (and re-validate the calibration, which was done at 60) or delete it from defaults.yaml.

AUDIT-TRAIL correlation_dimension.py:376-377: `_meta_correlation_dimension_eckmann_ruelle_slope_bound` is still emitted and reads 4.0 at N = 100 beside headline values of 5.4108068908 (gpt2), 5.9918865006 (distilgpt2) and 5.6591887179 (pythia-70m) that all carry status `ok`. The emitted bound therefore contradicts the emitted decision on 3 of 3 models, and my d-cube calibration shows the bound is empirically wrong for this estimator's small-radius window anyway (it recovers d = 8 at 6.1007 and d = 12 at 8.5445 from N = 100). The key should be dropped, not left as a number a reader will take for a validity limit. `d2_ceiling` inside the plateau helper is likewise computed and never used.

DEAD CODE correlation_dimension.py:316-318 and 219: `if False: pass else: ...` is a leftover from the atomic-branch removal, and `_atom_dominates` is initialised False and never reassigned, so `_meta_correlation_dimension_atom_dominates` is a constant-False column in every results file.

PROTOCOL correlation_dimension.py:110 `last_hidden = out.hidden_states[-1][0]`: this is `ln_f(block L-1)`, a LayerNorm output, not the deepest block's residual state, and no `_meta_last_entry_is_block_output` flag is emitted -- unlike the eleven tasks this campaign rewired, including topology_persistence_entropy and geometry_schatten, which both emit one. LayerNorm projects every row onto a fixed-radius shell and a correlation dimension is purely geometric, so the choice is material and model-dependent (a prior round measured gpt2 -18.5% and pythia-70m +48.3%, with the two models' ORDER reversed). Consistent with geometry_lid's convention for the same cloud, so I do not score it as a fidelity defect, but it must carry a provenance flag.

BOUNDARY (trivial) correlation_dimension.py:452: the pair floor is `C > 10/total` where the comment says a radius is usable 'once it contains enough pairs', i.e. >=. Exactly-10-pair radii are excluded.
fix: No change is required to the ESTIMAND -- the choice to drop the atomic switch and report the atom mass instead is correct and I endorse it. What must change is the wiring that would make the code compute the estimand the docstring describes: (1) when `_atom_frac > 0`, pass `distances[distances > 0]` to the promoted `_gp_correlation_dimension_plateau` for BOTH the headline and `_meta_correlation_dimension_continuous`, and set that `_meta_` key from the promoted kernel rather than the demoted percentile one -- measured cost of not doing so is -18.6% on a 4% point mass and -100% at 20%, and a -28.9% disagreement between the two keys. Add a direct regression for the 4% and 20% cases and for the one-duplicate case (which must stay at 2.65, not 0). (2) Wire the configured `num_radii` into both promoted calls or delete it from defaults.yaml: it currently names a 72% range and is inert. (3) Drop `_meta_correlation_dimension_eckmann_ruelle_slope_bound` and the unused `d2_ceiling`, which contradict the shipped decision on 3 of 3 models. (4) Remove the `if False:` block and either set or delete `_atom_dominates`. (5) Emit `_meta_last_entry_is_block_output` for the point cloud, as this task's siblings do. Outside the verdict: raise the effective point count above N = 100 (or report the bootstrap sd, for which the machinery already exists) before the value is used to order models.
